text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's Port Harcourt refinery operation control unit damaged; production output drops to 50 percent.

- Military administrators in the 36 states swear into office over 600 councillors and chairmen who emerged victorious in the municipal council polls conducted a fortnight ago. Others will take their oaths after by-elections.
- Central Bank says forex purchased from the autonomous foreign exchange market (AFEM) by commercial and merchant banks and not utilised within 10 working days must be returned to it.
- Chevron Nigeria, a unit of Chevron Corp, wants a review of memorandum of understanding between the military government and oil companies operating in the country.
- Electoral commission spent about 760 million naira to print voters' cards and conduct municipal elections, paper says, quoting own investigation.
- Eight African countries arrive in northern Nigerian city of Kaduna to begin preparations for Organisation of African Unity's trade fair, starting this weekend.

- Nigerian stock exchange lifts ban on trading on share price of airline operator Aviation Development Company (ADC). Ban was imposed in November after one of ADC jets crashed into a mangrove swamp near Lagos, killing all 142 on board.
- Nigerian Export-Import bank goes into distress six years after it was set up to help shore up volume of the country's non-oil exports.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha, at a dinner for businessmen in the capital Abuja, says the draft constitution approved in 1995 is already being implemented side by side with military decrees.
- Lecturers in southwestern Obafemi Awolowo University begin a three-day strike on Monday to protest at what they call gross under-funding of the institution and poor conditions of service.
